name: Box Breathing
description: A calming technique using equal-length inhale, hold, exhale, and hold phases to activate the parasympathetic nervous system.
steps: Find a comfortable seated position
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 counts
Hold your breath for 4 counts
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 4 counts
Hold empty for 4 counts
Repeat for 3-5 minutes

name: Body Scan
description: A progressive relaxation technique that draws awareness to each part of the body, releasing tension and building interoceptive awareness.
steps: Lie down or sit comfortably and close your eyes
Bring attention to the top of your head
Slowly move awareness down through your face, neck, shoulders
Continue through arms, chest, abdomen, hips
Move through legs, knees, feet, toes
Notice any sensations without judging them
Breathe into areas of tension and release

name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
description: A sensory grounding exercise that anchors awareness to the present moment through the five senses, useful for anxiety and overwhelm.
steps: Name 5 things you can see around you
Name 4 things you can physically feel
Name 3 things you can hear
Name 2 things you can smell
Name 1 thing you can taste
Take a deep breath and notice how you feel

name: Loving-Kindness Meditation
description: A compassion-focused meditation that cultivates warmth toward self and others through repeated phrases of well-wishing.
steps: Sit comfortably and close your eyes
Bring to mind someone you care about
Silently repeat: May you be happy, may you be healthy, may you be safe
Now direct those wishes toward yourself
Extend the wishes to a neutral person, then to someone difficult
Finally, extend to all beings everywhere

name: Mindful Breathing
description: The foundational mindfulness practice of observing the breath without trying to change it, building present-moment awareness.
steps: Sit in a comfortable position with a straight spine
Close your eyes or soften your gaze
Bring attention to your natural breathing rhythm
Notice the sensation of air at your nostrils or chest rising
When your mind wanders, gently return attention to the breath
Continue for 5 minutes without judgement

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
description: Systematically tensing and releasing muscle groups to reduce physical tension and promote awareness of the stress-relaxation contrast.
steps: Start with your feet: tense the muscles for 5 seconds
Release and notice the contrast for 10 seconds
Move to calves, then thighs, repeating tense-and-release
Continue through abdomen, chest, hands, arms, shoulders
Finish with face muscles: scrunch and release
Take a few deep breaths and notice your whole body

name: Reflective Journaling
description: Guided writing prompts that help externalize thoughts, identify patterns, and process emotions through structured self-reflection.
steps: Find a quiet space with pen and paper or a device
Write freely for 2 minutes about how you feel right now
Re-read what you wrote and circle recurring themes
Write about one theme: what triggered it, how it affects you
End by writing one small thing you can do about it today

name: Mindful Walking
description: A movement-based mindfulness practice that brings full attention to the sensations of walking, combining physical activity with present-moment awareness.
steps: Choose a short path, indoors or outdoors
Begin walking at a slower pace than normal
Focus on the sensation of your feet contacting the ground
Notice the shift of weight from heel to toe
If your mind wanders, gently return focus to the walking
After 10 minutes, stand still and take three deep breaths

name: Sleep Wind-Down Routine
description: A structured pre-sleep routine combining environmental cues and relaxation to improve sleep onset and quality.
steps: Set a consistent bedtime alarm 30 minutes before sleep
Put away screens and dim the lights
Do 5 minutes of gentle stretching
Practice box breathing or body scan for 5 minutes
Write down any lingering thoughts to externalize them
Lie down and focus on relaxing each body part

name: Mindful Social Connection
description: An exercise focused on deepening presence during social interactions through active listening and intentional engagement.
steps: Choose one conversation today to be fully present in
Put away your phone and face the person
Listen without planning your response
Notice their facial expressions and tone
Ask one genuine follow-up question
Afterwards, reflect on how being present felt
